title: Circular motion is the most stable Anthrobot behaviour; eclectic motion is transient

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Circular motion is the most stable Anthrobot behaviour; eclectic motion is transient

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In a Markov-chain model of transitions between movement types, circular motion is the most persistent Anthrobot behaviour, followed by linear and curvilinear motion, while eclectic motion acts as a transient intermediate that probabilistically resolves into one of the other three types.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We observed that the most stable movement pattern for an Anthrobot is circular motion, followed by linear/curvilinear motion. The eclectics act more like an intermediate and over time, at least probabilistically, resolve into one of the 3 other categories.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types”. Scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots, 30 s trajectory segments over 5 h

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The persistence ranking and transition claim map directly to a transition matrix. Public computational materials permit a substantial check, while classification dependence and incomplete raw coverage remain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reclassify sequential 30-second trajectory blocks and estimate transition matrices with uncertainty to compare self-transition probabilities and destinations from eclectic states.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Transitions may reflect classifier noise rather than behavioral switching.

Selected videos may not reproduce full-cohort probabilities.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.94
discriminating power: 0.74
data adequacy: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A transition matrix among movement labels is a standard calculation and would rank persistence if the segment labels were public. They are not. The result also depends on the unpublished clustering step, so neither the rank order nor the intermediate status of eclectic motion can be recomputed now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From labeled 30-second segments, estimate the Markov transition matrix among circular, linear, curvilinear and eclectic states over the five-hour recordings. Circular self-transition highest, and eclectic outflow into the other three states, would support the stability order; a high eclectic self-transition, or frequent circular-to-linear switches, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stability ranks inherit whatever cluster boundaries were chosen upstream.

Segment labels and the transition counts are not deposited.

The eclectic class is defined as whatever is left over, so its role as an intermediate is partly by construction.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.86
data existence: 0.15
data adequacy: 0.14
